extracted.intended_audience: general readers and film fans researching the film
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedia-style article summarizing a single film's production credits, plot, cast, background, release history, and reception. Used to inform readers about the film's details and critical/commercial performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Box office gross and records (e.g., '$2.2 million' box office; set records for the IFC Center's biggest opening weekend and the highest per-screen average for a first-time American filmmaker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial performance figures and noted exhibition records are used as indicators of the film's market success (first weekend limited theatrical release, per-screen averages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival premieres and screenings
rubrics_metrics.description: Festival appearances and status (e.g., world premiere at the Sundance Film Festival on January 23, 2012, in the NEXT category; screened at SXSW, Seattle International Film Festival, Nantucket, Independent Film Festival of Boston, BAMcinemaFest, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival selection and placement (premieres, opening-night films, centerpiece films) are cited as markers of industry recognition and exposure; specific festival awards (see awards metric) also matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival awards / jury/audience awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards received at festivals (e.g., won the Best of NEXT Audience Award at Sundance; won Best Writer/Director at Nantucket Film Festival).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival awards and audience prizes are presented as evidence of critical/audience approval and can be used to assess the film's prestige within the festival circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregator critical score — Rotten Tomatoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotten Tomatoes approval rating and average rating (e.g., '84% approval rating based on 117 reviews, with an average rating of 7.1/10') and the site's 'critics consensus' summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregated approval percentage, average numeric rating, and the written critics' consensus are treated as composite indicators of critical reception; the consensus text highlights perceived strengths/weaknesses (e.g., 'Laugh-out-loud funny and endearingly messy...overcomes its tonal inconsistencies').

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregator critical score — Metacritic
rubrics_metrics.description: Metacritic weighted average score (e.g., '71 out of 100 based on reviews from 28 critics') and its qualitative label ('generally favorable reviews').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metacritic's weighted average and qualitative interpretation are cited as another quantitative measure of critical reception, complementary to Rotten Tomatoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception and published reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual notable reviews and critical praise (e.g., The New York Times called the one-man show 'simply perfect'; Film.com praised the film as honestly portraying the life of a stand-up; Time Out named the stage show 'Show of the Year').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotations and summaries from prominent outlets and year-end lists are used to demonstrate critical endorsement and contextualize the film's cultural standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards, nominations and year-end lists beyond festivals
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry nominations and placements on critics' lists (e.g., Birbiglia nominated for Breakthrough Actor at the Gotham Independent Film Awards; film nominated for Best Art House Film by St. Louis Film Critics Association; named one of the Top Ten Independent Films of 2012 by the National Board of Review; various year-end list placements and reader polls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards nominations and inclusion on year-end critics' lists and reader polls are recorded as markers of broader critical recognition and legacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source material and development background
rubrics_metrics.description: Origins and adaptation information (e.g., film was co-written/directed/starring Mike Birbiglia; based on Birbiglia's autobiographical one-man show and a book; an excerpt aired on This American Life and Ira Glass collaborated on the film).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background on source material, theatrical origins, and creative collaborators is presented to explain the film's genesis and creative credibility; useful when evaluating faithfulness to source or the filmmaker's intent.
